target.title: fix(session): stop repeated restart recovery after retry budget
target.body:
Related: #95750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a gateway restart loop where the same interrupted main session can be accepted for automatic recovery on every boot. Supervisor backoff does not make the session healthy, so attempts separated by minutes or hours must still consume one durable recovery budget.

## Why This Change Was Made

Main-session restart recovery now has one canonical persisted fuse: `SessionEntry.mainRestartRecovery`.

- `automaticAttempts` counts accepted or acceptance-uncertain automatic recoveries since the last non-aborted run settlement on the same session.
- The first three recoveries may dispatch. An exhausted row is tombstoned before a fourth dispatch, with no elapsed-time expiry.
- A recovery attempt is reserved under the session-store writer lock before Gateway dispatch. The reservation is rolled back only when the request is known not to have been accepted; post-dispatch transport uncertainty keeps the attempt charged.
- Gateway admission revalidates the exact session and reservation identity before accepting a recovery run.
- Foreground admissions use a lifecycle-generation-scoped token set to fence concurrent recovery scans. Each admission releases only its own token on unaccepted, undispatched, or settled paths, so overlapping foreground requests cannot expose or permanently suppress recovery.
- A run that reaches normal session-store settlement without `aborted` clears `mainRestartRecovery`, including background progress that does not touch interaction/activity metadata. Session replacement and reset also clear it.
- `restartRecoveryRuns` remains lifecycle suppression only; it is not used to derive the durable retry budget.
- Subagent orphan recovery retains its separate policy: two attempts in the existing two-minute rapid re-wedge window.
- Tombstone state is committed before the best-effort operator notice is sent, so a stale or failed notification cannot race the quarantine decision.
- Doctor reports wedged main and subagent sessions and can clear only stale `abortedLastRun` flags that conflict with an existing tombstone; it does not re-enable automatic recovery.
- Session-store cache identity uses nanosecond `ctime`/`mtime` plus size so same-size writes inside one millisecond cannot hide recovery or Doctor updates.

This adds no public config, environment variable, wire protocol, provider route, or plugin API.

## User Impact

A wedged main session can no longer trigger unbounded automatic resume across Gateway restarts. After three accepted or acceptance-uncertain recovery attempts, OpenClaw quarantines the session before another automatic dispatch and asks the operator to inspect it and use `/new` or reset.

Healthy progress restores the full budget. The fuse does not expire merely because time passes.

## Evidence

Current branch:

```text
base: upstream/main@99ddde87262
head: 2408915c9ce
```

Current-head local static proof:

```text
node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --write src/gateway/server-methods/agent.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/agent.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts
git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD
.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base upstream/main
```

The final autoreview reported no accepted/actionable findings. Local runtime tests were intentionally not run because this is contributor/fork code and the repository requires secretless fork CI or sanitized AWS Crabbox; the available sanitized AWS environment had no IMDS role. Exact-head fork CI is therefore the runtime gate for `2408915c9ce`.

Focused regression coverage in the branch includes:

- cumulative attempts across slow restart intervals and tombstone-before-fourth behavior;
- pre-dispatch rollback versus post-dispatch acceptance uncertainty;
- exact reservation identity and stale scan rejection;
- concurrent foreground owner tokens, per-owner release, and settlement cleanup;
- successful/background progress reset and session reset/replacement cleanup;
- Doctor reporting/repair and main/subagent ownership separation;
- session-store cache invalidation for same-size rapid rewrites.

Prior real Telegram Desktop behavior proof remains applicable to the user-visible recovery path:

- Workflow: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28780448010
- Artifact bundle: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28780448010/artifacts/8106022765
- Manifest: https://artifacts.openclaw.ai/mantis/telegram-desktop/pr-96230/run-28780448010-1/index.json

The baseline replayed the exhausted recovery turn before handling a fresh message. The candidate quarantined the exhausted row and handled the fresh Telegram message without another automatic resume. Exact-head CI after the final rebase remains required before merge.
